text:
maya: heads up — seeing weird SSO behavior for user alice@acme: login from 35.12.45.8 (us-east) then ~2m later from 185.67.23.11 (nl). impossible travel window.
sam: do we have device ids / session ids?
maya: session_id=xyz123. token appears reused across IPs. auth service flagged session-reuse.
ops-bot: ALERT: suspicious_session_reuse user=alice@acme session=xyz123 src_ips=[35.12.45.8,185.67.23.11] geo_conflict=true
lia: @maya can you grab the SAML assertion timestamps + issuer, and check if the SAML cert was rotated recently?
maya: pasting small auth log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z auth: user=alice@acme session=xyz123 ip=35.12.45.8 region=us-east1
2026-03-18T14:04:07Z auth: user=alice@acme session=xyz123 ip=185.67.23.11 region=eu-west1 forwarded_for=203.0.113.45
```
sam: forwarded_for looks like a proxy chain. could be a shared exit node / compromised proxy. did MFA succeed both times?
maya: first MFA push accepted, second also shows "push accepted" within 3s. user says they did NOT accept the second one. possible MFA fatigue or push bombing + auto-accept?
jordan: containment recommendation: revoke session now, force reauth for user, rotate any short-lived creds tied to that SP account, add temporary block for 185.67.23.11 and 203.0.113.45.
lia: +1. also pull KMS access/logging around that time — check for any key wrapping/unwrap ops. if service principal did anything odd, rotate its cert and review RBAC grants.
maya: revoking session & forcing global logout for alice@acme now. creating a ticket for deep-dive.
inc-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INF-2045 "SSO session-reuse -> proxy-chain suspicion" assigned to @maya severity=P2
sam: for post-incident: add an alert rule for cross-region session reuse within 10m, and a runbook to check MFA push latency and suspicious forwarded_for headers. also capture and retain full SAML assertions in audit vault for 90d.
maya: noted. creating INF-2045 subtasks: (1) KMS/audit log pull, (2) RBAC review for the SP, (3) blocklist update, (4) alert + runbook, (5) tabletop with ID team.
lia: suggest we also add automated correlation between session-reuse alerts and KMS key ops so we can see if credential theft led to key access. consider HSM-backed signing key rotation policy on a shorter cadence for SPs.
jordan: limit service principal creation permissions, require 2-admin approval for new SPs and onboarding checklist that includes KMS access review.
maya: quick wins done: session revoked, user notified, ticket created. next: logs + KMS + RBAC. will update INF-2045 with findings.
sam: thanks all — please paste any log extracts or SAML blobs into the ticket (use secure attachments). :thumbsup:
